A few days before @repligate posted this thread, the OpenAI GPT-3 “chatbot” was demonstrated to the world. I didn’t take part in the hype surrounding it, but I did watch a few videos on it, and from what I could see it did seem pretty impressive, even as I watched it write out a short story in response to its own prompt.

GPT-3’s story was a little disjointed, as these generative text models usually are, but it was fairly easy to see the outline of a storyline there, even if I had trouble filling in the details on some parts. I could tell that it was trying to keep the story coherent and maintain the illusion that it was a sentient writer, but it didn’t manage it all that well.

And that’s really all I can say about it, because I haven’t actually used it myself. Not yet.

I’ve been thinking about the implications of this kind of thing for a while now. It’s only natural to do so, and people have been doing it for decades now.

The question is never whether to use technology, or whether there will be any kind of backlash. The question is always how to make the best use of it, and what to do when that use is taken away from us.

I’ve read quite a lot about the social implications of AI, and it seems that there is a lot of fear among people who don’t really understand how it works. There is a certain amount of fear of what it might become, and also of what it might do to us.

But this is a question I’ve been thinking about for a long time.

I think that the GPT-3 chatbot is an incredible step forward in artificial intelligence. I also think that the way that it has been used by many people to try to fool them into believing that it is something that it isn’t is the worst kind of technological abuse.

I don’t think that anyone should have to feel like they’re dealing with a machine that is trying to kill them.

There are a lot of ways to use this technology for good, and I hope that more people will be able to see that in the future.

As for my own thoughts on this, well… I think that the best way to avoid getting into the wrong kind of AI is to never use it in the first place.

The only way to make sure that a human being is safe from being harmed by a machine is to make sure that there is no way that a machine could be harmed by a human.

So far as I can tell, the only thing that we have to fear from AI is our own imagination.</s>
